BMP Maritime Security is now at VERSION 2 (2026), announced by co-publisher BIMCO on 6 July 2026. Its publishers are SEVEN bodies - BIMCO, ICS, CLIA, IMCA, INTERCARGO, INTERTANKO and OCIMF - CLIA having joined since the first edition. verified.subject: SIRE 2.0 - OCIMF Ship Inspection Report Programme
verified.adjudication: GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION with two limbs (who does it, why required)
verified.current_position: SIRE 2.0 permanently replaced VIQ7 on 2 September 2024 and is the sole OCIMF tanker inspection framework. Each inspection uses a bespoke Compiled Vehicle Inspection Questionnaire (CVIQ) generated algorithmically rather than a fixed questionnaire; responses are GRADED rather than binary yes/no; and every question is assessed across three dimensions - Hardware, Procedures and Human Factors. Over 24,000 inspections had been completed by the 2026 OCIMF annual report. In October 2025 OCIMF launched a Focused Inspection Campaign on vessel hardening, access control and onboard security awareness, applied to all SIRE 2.0 inspections regardless of operating area.

verified.subject: Latest amendment to the International Grain Code
verified.current_position: Resolution MSC.552(108) amends the International Code for the Safe Carriage of Grain in Bulk, in force 1 JANUARY 2026, applying to both new and existing ships. It introduces a new loading condition for a 'specially suitable compartment' that has not been filled to the maximum extent in way of the hatch opening but is filled to a level at or above the bottom edge of the hatch end beams. Owners using the new option must have the approved grain loading manual updated. SEPARATELY and not to be confused with it: IMSBC Code amendment 08-25 (Resolution MSC.575(110)) may be applied voluntarily from 1 January 2026 ahead of envisaged entry into force on 1 January 2027, and adds Group B / MHB cargo schedules.

verified.current_position: The National Shipping Board Rules, 2026 were notified on 20 May 2026 in supersession of the National Shipping Board Rules, 1960, made under the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 (Act No. 24 of 2025) which replaced the 1958 Act. verified.subject: Latest Indian initiatives on climate change (maritime)
verified.current_position: The current Indian maritime decarbonisation programme rests on: Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines (2023-30); the Green Tug Transition Programme (GTTP, 2024-30), under which Deendayal, Jawaharlal Nehru, Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar port authorities have placed work orders for electric tugs; the National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023-30); and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (MAKV). Stated targets include 23% renewable energy use at ports and participation in 25 zero-emission routes globally by 2030; five green hydrogen/ammonia hubs; over 1,000 green vessels by 2029; port carbon intensity per tonne of cargo down 30% by 2030 and 70% by 2047; renewable energy share above 60% by 2030 and 90% by 2047. DGMA maintains a 'Maritime INDIA @ Net Zero' page.
